title: AI in Sensory and the QA System
author: Ankur Napa
summary: The final part of the brewery-lab AI series: taster notes as data via NLP, a predictive freshness index, predictive calibration from instrument drift, and deviation and out-of-spec triage. Honest about where a confident model quietly misleads.

title: Machine Vision on the Packaging Line
author: Ankur Napa
summary: Inline machine vision on the brewery packaging line: fill-level checks with SPC to catch drift, crown-seal and label-defect inspection, washed-bottle grading, and pasteurisation-unit modelling from tunnel temperatures.

title: From Plate Counts to Risk Triage in Microbiology
author: Ankur Napa
summary: How AI earns its keep in brewery micro: contamination-risk triage that ranks sample points across propagation, packaging, water and CIP, plus vision colony counting. Honest about where it breaks.

title: Soft Sensors in the Beer-Chemistry Lab
author: Ankur Napa
summary: Part 3 of the brewery-lab AI series: diacetyl and VDK forecasting from the fermentation curve, dissolved-oxygen anomaly detection at the filler, and shelf-life survival models, with the reference method still the arbiter.

title: On the Malt Bench: Vision, NIR and Incoming QC
author: Ankur Napa
summary: How machine vision reads acrospire growth, malt colour and foreign material on the raw-materials bench, and how NIR soft sensors predict extract and moisture before the mash, with the honest caveats.

title: AI in the Brewery Lab: What's Real and What's Hype
author: Ankur Napa
summary: A map of where AI genuinely fits in the brewery QC lab in 2026 (soft sensors, machine vision, contamination-risk triage, and predictive calibration) and where a confident model quietly breaks. The opening of a 6-part series that walks the lab bench by bench.

title: I Built a Global Beer Sensory Tool on Microsoft Fabric (with Rayfin)
author: Ankur Napa
summary: A working tool where breweries' tasters share sensory feedback and everyone sees how each batch drifts from its style's world ideal. It's built on Microsoft Fabric, with the backend deployed in one command using Rayfin.

title: Saving Water in a Brewery: Data Analytics vs AI vs Generative AI
author: Ankur Napa
summary: Three different tools, one goal: a lower water-to-beer ratio. Where plain data analytics, machine-learning AI, and generative AI each genuinely cut brewery water use — and where each one is the wrong tool.

title: Modeling a Maltery as a Digital Twin on Microsoft Fabric
author: Ankur Napa
summary: After the brewery, the maltery. A live 3D digital twin of the whole malting process — intake, steeping, germination, kilning, deculming, malt storage and dispatch — built on Microsoft Fabric with the Rayfin SDK, every vessel clickable for its real process curve.

title: Modeling a Brewery in 3D: Procedural Vessels and Process Flow (Part 2)
author: Ankur Napa
summary: Part 2 of building a brewery digital twin: how I modeled every vessel — mash tun, lauter tun, kettle, cylindro-conical fermenters — from code instead of Blender, drove the whole plant from one process-data file, and animated the flow between tanks. With an honest take on when Blender is the right call.

title: What AI in Beer Actually Looks Like in 2026
author: Ankur Napa
summary: Beyond the headlines about AI-designed beer: what artificial intelligence is genuinely doing in breweries in 2026 — recipe ideation, batch consistency, a brewers' chatbot, and the supply chain — and where the hype quietly breaks.

title: I Turned My Brewery Into a 3D Digital Twin on Microsoft Fabric
author: Ankur Napa
summary: Not a dashboard you read — a brewery you walk through. How I rebuilt Ankur Napa Brewing Company as a live 3D digital twin on Microsoft Fabric, shipped in an afternoon with the Rayfin SDK, with every vessel and POS wired to real-time data.

title: Where Your Extract, Water and Energy Go: Sankey and the Brewhouse Balance
author: Ankur Napa
summary: A brewery's biggest losses hide in plain sight across a dozen separate reports. A Sankey diagram puts the whole mass and energy balance in one picture — extract from grain to glass, water in to effluent out, energy in to heat lost — so the leaks become impossible to miss.

title: Shelf-Life Trajectories: Visualizing Forced-Ageing and Flavour Stability
author: Ankur Napa
summary: A beer's flavour stability is a story over time, not a single number — yet most breweries record it as a pass/fail. How to visualize forced-ageing and shelf-life trials as trajectories and small multiples, so staling becomes a path you can see, compare and predict.

title: SPC That Actually Catches Drift: Capability, CUSUM and EWMA for Brewers
author: Ankur Napa
summary: The Shewhart control chart catches sudden spikes but is blind to slow drift — exactly how brewing quality usually fails. How process capability (Cp/Cpk), CUSUM and EWMA charts visualize the slow creep a basic control chart misses, in brewing terms.

title: True-to-Target: Visualizing Whether a Batch Matches Its Brand Profile
author: Ankur Napa
summary: True-to-target (TTT) tasting asks a different question than 'is it in spec' — does this batch still taste like the brand? How to visualize brand conformance with radar profiles, target bands and deviation tracking, so a panel's verdict becomes a picture the whole brewery reads.

title: Beyond the Control Chart: Data Visualizations Brewers Underuse
author: Ankur Napa
summary: Most brewery dashboards stop at the line chart and the control chart. This opens a series on the visualizations brewers rarely reach for — radar brand-profiles, CUSUM drift charts, shelf-life trajectories and Sankey balances — and how to match the chart to the brewing question.

title: Vibe-Coding a Fermentation Tracker: A Brewer's Build Log
author: Ankur Napa
summary: A concrete, step-by-step build log of vibe-coding a small fermentation tracker with Claude Fable 5 — the actual prompts, the verify steps, the bug it introduced and how it got caught, so you can copy the loop for your own brewery tool.

title: What Claude Fable 5 Changes for Brewers Who Build
author: Ankur Napa
summary: Anthropic's latest model, Claude Fable 5, doesn't replace the brewer's judgement — it lowers the skill floor for building. What actually changes for a brewer making their own tools, what doesn't, and how to use it without fooling yourself.

title: Vibe-Coding a Brewing Tool with Claude Fable 5
author: Ankur Napa
summary: Claude's latest model, Fable 5, makes it realistic for a brewer with no software background to build a small, genuinely useful brewery tool by describing what they want. Here's the honest loop, what Fable 5 changes, and where it still needs you.

title: Generative and Human-Centred AI for Brewers (with Google's PAIR Guidebook)
author: Ankur Napa
summary: The final stage of the brewer's AI roadmap — using generative AI well and building with it responsibly, grounded in Google's PAIR People + AI Guidebook and Microsoft Learn's responsible-AI resources, so what you make is something a brewer would actually trust.

title: Your First Machine-Learning Model on Brewing Data (Free Courses)
author: Ankur Napa
summary: Stage 3 of the brewer's AI roadmap — the machine-learning concepts that matter, then building a first real model on your own brewery data, using free resources: Google's Machine Learning Crash Course, Kaggle Learn, Elements of AI and scikit-learn.

title: Foundations First: Data Literacy and Python for Brewers (Free Resources)
author: Ankur Napa
summary: Stages 1 and 2 of the brewer's AI roadmap — data literacy with spreadsheets and Power BI, then Python — using only free, open resources: Microsoft Learn, Kaggle Learn and freeCodeCamp, with a real brewing project to learn against.

title: A Brewer's Step-by-Step Roadmap into AI (with Free Resources)
author: Ankur Napa
summary: A practical, five-stage learning path for a working brewer who wants to get into AI — data literacy, spreadsheets to Power BI, Python, machine learning and generative AI — built entirely on free, open resources like Microsoft Learn, Kaggle and Google's PAIR guidebook.

title: The Translator: When the Winemaker Is Also the Power BI Developer
author: Ankur Napa
summary: What changes when one person has stood on the crush pad, run the ferments and pulled barrel samples — and also holds the Power BI and Microsoft Fabric certifications. Why the hybrid profile builds winery dashboards that survive a vintage, and the honest limits of being one.
